room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "pew-DEEK": a bashful girl blushes and hides her PUDDING cup behind her back: pew-DEEK ≈ PUD-eek
note: Modest, discreet about feelings or the body: un sourire pudique; une pudeur, modesty.

room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "an-dee-SEEBL": a girl's jaw drops at a gleaming model of the Capitol, IN D.C.: a sight beyond words: an-dee-SEEBL ≈ IN-D.C.-ble
note: Beyond words, for joy or for horror: une joie indicible, une souffrance indicible.

room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "lahn-see-NAHN": Sir LANCElot, in shining armor, holds up a red, THROBBING sore thumb and winces: lahn-see-NAHN ≈ LANCE-a-lot
note: Throbbing, shooting (pain); also nagging or haunting of a worry or a tune: une douleur lancinante, une question lancinante.

room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "see-noh-NEEM": the teacher chalks FAST and QUICK on the blackboard: two words, one meaning, SYNONYMS: see-noh-NEEM = SYNONYM
note: As an adjective: « rapide » est synonyme de « vite ». More often a masculine noun: un synonyme, a synonym (opposite: un antonyme).

room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "lew-DEEK": LOU fans out his DECK of cards and starts a game for the kids: lew-DEEK ≈ LOU-DECK
note: To do with play or games: une activité ludique, une approche ludique (a playful way to learn).

room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "kahl-KEHR": a carton of milk, full of CALcium, spills over a big white LIMESTONE block: kahl-KEHR ≈ CAL-cium
note: Limestone, chalky: une roche calcaire; of water, hard: l'eau calcaire. As a masculine noun, le calcaire is limestone, or limescale in a kettle.

room_name: La cantine des scolaires · The field-trip lunchroom
hook: "shahr-NEHL": a cheerful boy rubs a stick of CHARcoal up his bare arm until the skin is smudged gray: all about the body, the flesh: shahr-NEHL ≈ CHAR-NEL
note: Of the body and the senses: l'amour charnel, un lien charnel (a bond of flesh and blood). Do not confuse it with its grim relative le charnier, a mass grave.
